newsitem.title: INDIA: Pakistan, India end talks, agree to meet again.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan, India end talks, agree to meet again.

text.p: Indian and Pakistani diplomats ended four days of talks on Monday and in a sign of a thaw in frosty relations between the neighbours said they would meet again in the Pakistan capital Islamabad.

"The two foreign secretaries discussed all outstanding issues of concern to both sides in a frank, cordial and constructive manner," a joint statement issued at the end of the talks said. "The foreign secretaries decided to continue their discussions in Islamabad on dates to be mutually decided."
Indian Foreign Secretary Salman Haidar and his Pakistani counterpart Shamshad Ahmad, who held lengthy discussions at Haidar's residence on Sunday, completed their negotiations earlier on Monday.

The two diplomats' joint statement ended an official silence imposed on the talks, the first since a similar dialogue collapsed in acrimony three years ago over the divided Himalayan region of Kashmir.

The talks have coincided with renewed violence in Kashmir and political turmoil in New Delhi, where the Congress party on Sunday withdrew support for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 10-month-old minority coalition government.
